statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures are rotating inside a narrow overnight range after a strong Monday cash session, and mean reversion currently remains available.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold during Asian hours. The published danger window covers the US cash open and late morning on 22 September, where continuation risk after Monday's gap-and-go session is concentrated.
headline: Orderly overnight range follows a 2.83% Nasdaq-100 advance; conditional risk concentrated at the US cash open
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday 21 September at 30,482.35, up 2.83%, in a 29,933.22-30,557.33 range that never traded back to the prior 29,644.17 close, finishing 0.25% below the session high. The Nasdaq Composite posted a record close at 27,122.09. Leadership was concentrated in semiconductors for a fifth consecutive session, with Intel up about 12%, AMD about 10% and crossing a one trillion dollar market value, Qualcomm above 9% and Arm about 17%, after early indications of success for Meta's Muse AI agent lifted expectations for AI compute demand. Cross-assets were supportive rather than stressed: Brent fell 2.04% to 101.71 dollars and WTI to about 98.20 dollars on hopes of US-Iran diplomacy around the UN General Assembly, Treasury yields eased from the 18 September H.15 readings of 4.76% at two years and 5.01% at ten years, and the VIX finished at 14.87 in a 14.60-15.13 range with no volatility bid. Front Nasdaq-100 futures are currently near 30,876 inside a narrow overnight range of roughly 110 points, holding the upper half but rotating two-way. That combination, a strong aligned uptrend but orderly, retracing overnight price discovery and very low implied volatility, keeps Tail low for the current hour. The forward path is the live question: an aligned bullish regime meeting the opening auction is the specific structure that has previously denied mean reversion, so conditional Tail rises into the 13:30 UTC cash open and peaks in the US late morning before easing. Tuesday's own macro calendar is light, with the Richmond Fed index and Fed speakers rather than a tier-1 release; the week's first high-impact US data is the S&P Global flash PMI set on 23 September.

lookbackSummary: Over the previous 24 clock hours the published Claude path started in the low band through the Asian session on 21 September, stepped into trend-up from the European open, crossed into the watch band around 11:00 UTC and into the block band from 14:00 UTC as the US cash session produced a sustained one-way advance, peaking at Tail 33 in the 19:00 UTC hour. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the path decayed quickly, returning to the low band by 21:00 UTC and to normal mode overnight as price discovery became orderly.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours keep the low band through the Asian and European sessions on 22 September, with conditional risk building into the US cash open at 13:30 UTC. The published danger window runs 13:30-17:00 UTC, peaking at Tail 27 in the 15:00 UTC hour, reflecting the conditional risk that an aligned bullish regime extends from the opening auction with shallow pullbacks. Scores ease from 17:00 UTC and return to the low band after the 20:00 UTC cash close. This forward path is conditional: it would be revised higher only on observed shallow or failed retracements and repeated extension, and lower on orderly two-way rotation.
